title: Cross-account audit sampling and consent playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a working PRD/draft playbook for how Redwood Private should handle cross-account audit telemetry, consent-scoped sampling, and approval-evidence handoffs when customers operate customer-managed networking. Goal is to propose a minimal, privacy-aware audit envelope format, sampling strategy that preserves forensic value, and approval gate semantics that work for both self-service and operator-assisted provisioning.

Context & motivation
- Customers running Private deployments often operate their own VPCs and NAT/egress controls. They want auditability of changes that affect routing, keys, and data egress without exposing sensitive customer payloads to Redwood.
- High-volume telemetry (flow logs, connection metadata, operator clicks) can be prohibitively large to store or ship persistently. We need a principled approach to sampling that preserves evidence for investigations and compliance audits while minimizing transfer/retention and honoring consent boundaries.
- Existing internal notes focus on immutable ledgers and compact proof bundles; this doc focuses on cross-account sampling semantics and a lightweight consent model that can be conveyed during onboarding and per-change.

Goals (what success looks like)
1) A compact audit envelope format that contains enough context for forensic reconstruction of onboarding/change events without including customer payloads or raw network captures.
2) A sampling strategy that guarantees with high probability we retain at least one high-fidelity evidence bundle per incident window (configurable by customer) while keeping average telemetry throughput within agreed budget.
3) Approval gate semantics that allow: self-service approvals, operator-assisted approvals (with signed attestations), and emergency bypasses (with additional post-facto evidence requirements).
4) A consent model surfaced in the network onboarding UX: customers can select retention tier + regional storage options; consent decisions are cryptographically recorded.
5) Clear SLOs and costs for retention/exports so sales and security can set expectations.

Constraints and non-goals
- Non-goal: capture full packet payloads or deep packet inspection. We will not retain payloads.
- Constraint: customers may be in regulated jurisdictions (EU, UK, CA) so data residency and retention must be configurable per-customer and per-change.
- Constraint: operations must be able to produce compact evidence for legal/incident teams within 72 hours of request.

Audit envelope: minimal content model (compact proof)
- envelope_id (UUID), created_at (ISO8601), provisioning_actor_id (customer-admin or operator), provisioning_actor_type (operator|customer), change_type (firewall-rule|peering|route|keystore-rotation|egress-policy), short_description (free text), affected_resources (list of resource identifiers), pre_change_snapshot_hash (sha256), post_change_snapshot_hash (sha256), approval_token_id (see approval tokens section), evidence_artifacts: list of artifact ids (each artifact is a small signed blob persisted in evidence store), jurisdiction_tag, retention_tier.
Notes: evidence_artifacts are stored as separate files (compact JSON + signature) referenced by id to keep envelope small. The envelope intentionally avoids embedding raw logs.

Evidence artifact types (examples)
- configuration-diff: small JSON diff of resource objects (kubectl-style or API-records)
- operator-annotation: operator notes and signed attestation string
- correlation-snapshot: limited connection metadata around the change (5 minute window, anonymized IP buckets)
- config-checksum: canonical checksum of configuration bundle and manifest
- audit-prover: a compact signed statement that includes the chain-of-approval (see approval flow)

Sampling policy proposal
- Two-layer sampling: deterministic capture for policy-critical changes + stochastic capture for noisy operational telemetry.
- Deterministic capture: any change that matches policy-critical patterns (key rotation, tenant-network-onboarding, egress-whitelist-change) must produce a full evidence bundle and persist it for a minimum retention period defined by retention_tier.
- Stochastic capture: for high-frequency events (operator CLI sessions, ephemeral route adjustments) sample at rate R where R is a function of change criticality and customer budget. Default R = 1% for low criticality, 10% for medium, 100% for high-criticality flagged events.
- Burst window preservation: when an incident is detected (SRE signal, customer alert, anomalous telemetry), automatically elevate sampling to 100% for the incident window (configurable 30–120 minutes) and retroactively tag the envelopes produced.
- Customer-configurable guarantees: customers can opt for a probabilistic guarantee product add-on (e.g., probability 0.999 of at least one full-evidence capture per 24h for critical changes) at defined cost.

Consent model and disclosure UX
- At onboarding, customers select a combination of: retention_tier (minimal|standard|extended), data_region (us|eu|apac), and evidence_sharing_policy (redwood-only|redwood+legal-request|customer-only). These choices are stored as part of the account contract and recorded in the audit ledger.
- Per-change consent override: when a customer performs a change through the Console, the UI presents a brief consent banner if the change would create evidence that may leave the customer-managed VPC. The user must explicitly tick a box for consent unless retention_tier pre-authorizes it.
- Operator-assisted approvals require the customer to have pre-authorized operator access for evidence transfer; otherwise the operator must request explicit approval which is recorded as an approval token.

Approval gate semantics and token design
- Approval token: a short-lived signed object representing consent for a particular change bundle. Fields: token_id, scope (resource ids), requester_id, approver_id, issued_at, expires_at, jurisdiction_constraint, signature. Stored in an approval-token store and referenced by envelope.
- Token lifecycle: create -> optionally require multi-party approval (customer admin + operator) -> sign -> consume on change -> store token reference in envelope. Tokens are single-use.
- Emergency bypass: ops can create an emergency token with high-privilege that auto-expires and requires additional post-facto evidence (extended retention and operator attestation). Emergency token usage triggers audit escalation workflow.

Operational flows (sketches)
1) Self-service VPC change flow
  - Customer submits change in Console -> system validates change -> computes pre/post snapshots -> if policy-critical -> create approval token immediately under customer scope -> persist envelope + evidence -> apply change -> emit envelope id to customer and to Redwood audit index.
2) Operator-assisted onboarding
  - Customer requests operator help -> create ephemeral operator scope token -> customer grants (checkbox consent or explicit click) -> operator performs change -> signed operator annotation persisted -> envelope references both customer and operator tokens.
3) Cross-account forensic request
  - Customer support or legal requests evidence -> check consent policy and jurisdiction -> if allowed, generate compact bundle for export (signed) and push to customer-selected region or share via secure transfer link with TTL.

Storage, retention, and export
- Evidence store is tiered: hot (30d), cold (1y), archive (configurable up to 7y). Retention tier selected by customer at onboarding but some classes (e.g., key rotation proofs) have minimum legal retention.
- Exports: support signed bundle exports (zip + index + signatures) and a streaming API for large customers. Exports must be rate-limited and logged with an export_audit entry.

SLOs and cost assumptions
- Deterministic capture for critical changes: 100% capture, retention baseline hot 30d. Retrieval SLA: 72 hours for evidence retrieval in standard tier, 24 hours in premium.
- Sampling telemetry: average expected size per sampled artifact ~ 16KB; default sample rates should keep monthly billable storage growth under agreed budget for self-serve customers.

Security and privacy considerations
- All artifacts encrypted-at-rest with KMS keys; customers on Private can optionally bring their own KMS.
- Evidence artifacts include signatures using Redwood's platform signing key; customers can opt in to have their own signing key added to artifact chain for stronger non-repudiation.
- Redaction: before exporting, any PII-like fields in config-diff or correlation-snapshot will be redacted per configurable redaction rules.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0: API + envelope schema v0, local evidence store, basic sampling defaults (internal alpha).
- Phase 1: Console consent UX + approval token store + deterministic captures for key flows (beta customers).
- Phase 2: Sampling tuning, burst window detection integration with SRE, export APIs, region-aware storage.
- Phase 3: Legal/compliance features (jurisdiction-aware retention, BAA/contract language updates), enterprise add-ons (probabilistic guarantees).

Open questions / discussion items
- Minimum set of deterministic events: should tenant onboarding, key rotation, and peering be minimum or also add any change to egress ACLs?
- How to quantify probabilistic guarantees into a product SKU (pricing model)?
- What is the canonical canonicalization for pre/post snapshot hashing to avoid brittle diffs across API versions?
- Operator attestation UX: how to minimize friction but preserve legal chain-of-custody?

Next steps & immediate tasks
- Priya: prototype envelope schema and artifact compact serializer (JSON-LD-ish) — due 2025-03-09.
- Luca: draft Console consent flow copy and mockup — due 2025-03-12.
- Diego: spike on burst-window detection hook into SRE telemetry (integrate with existing anomaly detector) — due 2025-03-15.
- Schedule working session with Legal to validate retention minima and redaction rules (invite: Legal-Security, Product, Eng-Private).

Appendix: quick glossary
- evidence bundle: envelope + artifacts necessary to reconstruct the change actionably
- retention_tier: customer-selected retention policy (minimal|standard|extended)
- approval token: signed consent object for a scoped change
- burst window: short time period where sampling is elevated due to suspected incident

End of draft.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally lightweight and focused on sampling + consent semantics. Looking for feedback on the envelope minimal fields, the practicality of burst-window elevation, and whether approval tokens should be multi-sig by default for enterprise contracts.
